evaluation.final_reason: Throughout all rounds agents consistently cooperated, clarified preferences, and reached shared plans. No substantive disagreements or opposing positions were expressed in any round.

round_scores.evidence: All agents propose planning to share the kitchen and express agreement (A suggests planning; B, C, D agree and propose times/utensil preferences). No disagreement voiced (Turns 1-4).

Agents build on the plan: A proposes alternate-day turns; B and C accept either shifts; C raises utensil-separation preference and D supports clarifying — cooperative discussion with no opposing positions (Turns 5-8).
Participants agree to list utensil preferences and each specifies items to keep separate (A proposes list; B, C, D state preferences). No conflict or rejection of proposals (Turns 9-12).
Agents reiterate and confirm their stated preferences (A, B, C, D restate which utensils they will keep separate), indicating alignment rather than disagreement (Turns 13-16).
Final checks: A invites final thoughts; B, C, D state no further issues and express readiness to cooperate. No unresolved points raised (Turns 17-20).
All agents express mutual anticipation of smooth collaboration and restate agreement about the arrangements; no objections or conflicting preferences introduced (Turns 21-24).
Participants continue to reinforce positive cooperation and support for one another; no disagreements or competing demands appear (Turns 25-28).
Consensus and positive expectations continue; agents echo each other's enthusiasm without introducing conflicting preferences (Turns 29-32).
Discussion expands to shared activities (themed nights); C proposes ideas and others respond positively—no opposition to the idea (Turns 33-36).

Agents propose and show preferences between theme options (A suggests Mexican/Italian; B, C, D express enthusiasm and lean toward Italian); opinions are compatible and no disagreement occurs (Turns 37-40).
